---
title: "Exercise · Hands"
---

A short, guided task. Complete it before moving on to the lab. All snippets
use **provider-neutral capabilities**; no external accounts, tokens, or
network calls are required.

## Task

For a Pico you have been modeling across Part 3, write a capability-based
Hands declaration:

```yaml
# hands-capabilities.yaml
hands:
  - name: external
    capabilities:
      - github.issue.read
      - github.issue.create
  - name: cluster
    capabilities:
      - kubernetes.resource.read
```

Then write rules that govern the capabilities. Rules name capabilities, not
provider tools, and include an actor so authorization is identity-aware:

```yaml
# hands-rules.yaml
actor:
  pico: pico-alice
rules:
  - capability: github.issue.create
    effect: allow
  - capability: kubernetes.resource.delete
    effect: deny
```

Finally, sketch the **evidence** a Pico would keep after a single
`github.issue.create` invocation:

```yaml
# evidence-sample.yaml
evidence:
  actor: pico-alice
  capability: github.issue.create
  authorized-by: rule-1
  hand: external
  outcome: succeeded
  timestamp: 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z
```

Answer the reflection questions below.

::: {.callout-note}
There is no single correct answer. The goal is to internalize the
capability-over-provider model: rules name capabilities, not provider tool
names, so the provider can be swapped without changing Pico behaviour.
:::

## Success criteria

- [ ] Your Hands declaration is provider-neutral (no provider tool names such
      as `GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL`).
- [ ] You declare at least **two** capabilities across at least **one**
      hand/provider.
- [ ] Your rules name capabilities, not provider-specific tools.
- [ ] Your rules carry an `actor` — authorization is bound to an identity.
- [ ] At least one rule uses `effect: deny`.
- [ ] Your evidence sample records actor, capability, authorizing rule, hand,
      outcome, and timestamp.

## Automatable check

Save the three snippets under a scratch working directory and confirm they
parse. No external service is contacted.

```bash
mkdir -p scratch-hands
cat > scratch-hands/hands.yaml <<'EOF'
hands:
  - name: external
    capabilities:
      - github.issue.read
      - github.issue.create
rules:
  - capability: github.issue.create
    effect: allow
  - capability: kubernetes.resource.delete
    effect: deny
EOF
pico parse scratch-hands/hands.yaml --out /tmp/hands.json \
  && echo "OK: Hands declaration parses"
```

The command exits with status `0` and prints an `OK:` line when the
declaration is well-formed.

## Reflect

- Why would a rule say `email.send` rather than `GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL`?
- What does "a valid credential must not imply authorization" mean when
  Composer equipment and Open Engineering policy are separate concerns?
- Why is the evidence record kept even when the outcome is `succeeded`?
